title: Jensen Huang is out at Nvidia, and CFO Colette Kress steps in as interim CEO
summary: Jensen Huang has been ousted as CEO of Nvidia after reports that he had affairs with both an alleged Chinese spy and one of his direct reports, TechCrunch reported Thursday, November 12, 2026. Huang had been so central to the company that he never established a succession plan. While Nvidia conducts a more thorough search for a successor, CFO and Executive Vice President Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO of a company worth about $3.8 trillion. Kress, 59, has worked at Nvidia since September 2013, after three years as a CFO at Cisco and 13 years at Microsoft. “I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” Kress said in a statement, adding that the company’s focus remains on customers, partners, developers and shareholders. Nvidia is slated to report quarterly earnings on Tuesday, November 17, when Kress is likely to say more about her plans.

title: S&P 500 futures edge up as Nvidia steadies and Wall Street waits on producer prices
summary: Reuters reported Friday, November 13, 2026, that Nasdaq 100 futures were muted at the end of a volatile week that saw Jensen Huang resign as Nvidia’s CEO. At 6:33 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis rose 27 points, or 0.05%, S&P 500 E-minis gained 11.75 points, or 0.15%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis lost 7.5 points, or 0.03%. Nvidia rose 2.6% premarket after losing about 11% this week through Thursday, but is still on course for its longest streak of weekly losses since October 2012. Microsoft fell 2.1% after an Outlook, Teams and Copilot outage that stretched beyond 12 hours, while Cerebras jumped more than 17%. Investors are awaiting October’s producer price inflation reading; traders fully price in a Federal Reserve hike next month, with odds of a 50-basis-point move around 12%, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

title: Nvidia ticks higher premarket as investors weigh life after Jensen Huang
summary: CNBC reported that Nvidia shares were 1.8% higher as of 5:00 a.m. ET on Friday, November 13, 2026, as investors navigated the fallout from Jensen Huang’s resignation after reports of at least two affairs. The move followed a wild Thursday session in which the stock dropped sharply before recovering to close just over 4% lower. Huang resigned as CEO after The New York Times reported a romantic relationship with an Nvidia vice president, and he was already under scrutiny after a board investigation into his relationship with a businesswoman whom intelligence agencies say is a Chinese spy. Before Huang resigned, several Wall Street analysts told CNBC his departure could cost Nvidia as much as 20% of its market value, and the stock is already down more than 20% over the last month. ODDO BHF’s Stephane Houri said the issue reaches the “architecture of the AI industry.”

title: Cerebras jumps premarket after a surprise profit, a higher forecast and a Microsoft cloud deal
summary: Reuters reported that Cerebras Systems shares gained more than 14% in premarket trading on Friday, November 13, 2026, after the AI chipmaker raised its annual sales forecast and posted a surprise profit, a gain that would add over $3 billion to its market value if it holds. Cerebras now expects 2026 adjusted revenue of $940 million to $960 million, up from $880 million to $890 million, versus analysts’ average estimate of $887.04 million, according to LSEG. It reiterated plans to triple revenue in 2027 and said it signed a cloud deal with Microsoft, with details next year. Adjusted cloud and services revenue, which reflects its OpenAI deal, more than tripled to $144.9 million, and adjusted profit was $29.82 million, against an expected loss. As of Thursday’s close, the shares were down 47.2% from their May IPO price of $185.

title: Modine soars 31% premarket on a report that Samsung is in talks to buy the data center cooling maker
summary: Investing.com reported that Modine Manufacturing shares surged 31% in premarket trading on Friday, November 13, 2026, after Bloomberg reported that Samsung Electronics was in discussions to acquire the data center cooling systems maker, with a potential transaction possibly coming together within weeks. Modine has been sharpening its focus on climate solutions after spinning off its Performance Technologies segment, which was merged with Gentherm. Its data center business has been a major growth driver, with revenue rising 95% year over year in its latest quarter and quarterly orders reaching a record of more than $1 billion. The company has also launched a large-scale chiller manufacturing facility in Texas to serve demand for cooling systems used in AI data centers. In the same premarket roundup, S&P 500 futures were up 0.2% as of 6:07 a.m. ET.

title: Democrats open a second congressional probe into Nvidia’s China chip sales as Huang agrees to testify
summary: Rep. Richard Neal, the top Democrat on the House Ways and Means Committee, and Sen. Ron Wyden, the top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee, have launched an inquiry into Nvidia’s China sales and its dealings with the Trump administration, TechCrunch reported Thursday, November 12, 2026. Their letter asks Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to preserve records about an arrangement under which H200 chips bound for China were first shipped to the United States and tariffed, which the letter calls “an unconstitutional export tax system.” It also questions why Commerce let Singapore-based Megaspeed, whose executive is the alleged spy linked to Huang, keep buying chips. It is the second congressional investigation since the affair broke: a Republican-led group from three House committees demanded closed-door testimony, and on Thursday, after resigning, Huang agreed.

title: Anthropic will start trading as “ANT” on Thursday, November 19, in the AI trade’s next big test
summary: Anthropic’s shares will begin trading under the ticker symbol “ANT” on Thursday, November 19, 2026, Yahoo Finance reported Thursday, November 12. In an amended S-1 filing on Tuesday, the Claude maker said it expects to sell 825 million shares priced between $70 and $78, giving it a market valuation of between $1.3 trillion and $1.45 trillion. Anthropic was initially projected to come to market at a valuation as high as $2 trillion, but recent turmoil in the AI sector knocked that down. Revenue for the first nine months of the year reached $33.2 billion, compared with $4.6 billion for all of 2025, and operating losses narrowed to $1.3 billion from $5.2 billion a year earlier. The company also disclosed aggregate committed spending of $895.4 billion, primarily on compute and infrastructure. The listing could set the standard for OpenAI’s anticipated debut early next year.

title: AI chatbots sent shoppers to fake or risky retail sites in up to 15% of answers, study finds
summary: Shoppers using AI chatbots to research products could be directed to imposters and other risky websites, according to a study by IP protection firm Podqi shared with The Verge on Thursday, November 12, 2026. Podqi asked ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity shopping questions about 151 brands, such as “Where can I find [brand] online?”, during two testing periods in September. Across 6,795 answers, all three cited risky sites, defined as fake websites impersonating real retailers or selling knockoffs, old brand domains reregistered by someone else, or dead sites someone else could buy. Gemini showed risky sites least often, in 4% of answers, Perplexity the most, in 15%, and ChatGPT fell in the middle. Risky sites appeared more often when the AI was asked about regional brand websites. Ahead of holiday shopping, Podqi CEO Trevor West advised verifying the source before entering personal or credit card information.

title: Google brings its fast Gemini 4 Hydrogen model to Search for tougher, multi-part questions
summary: Google is rolling out Gemini 4 Hydrogen to all Search users globally, TechCrunch reported Thursday, November 12, 2026. While Google’s frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, are best at deep reasoning, Hydrogen is designed for fast execution across agentic workflows. Google says it completes tasks 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash, its previous fast model, and even beats Gemini 4 Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high thinking level. In Search, Hydrogen brings a better understanding of user intent, including multi-part questions and hard-to-understand typos, an improved fan-out technique that breaks one prompt into multiple subqueries, and more images, comparison tables and custom tools in AI Mode. It offers four thinking levels, low, medium, high and a new “xhigh,” and ranks No. 5 on Agent Arena’s benchmarks for multi-step tasks.

title: Edge0 open-sources a 145-billion-parameter model built to run on a laptop
summary: Edge0 on Thursday, November 12, 2026, open-sourced Edge0-145B and Edge0-120B, along with its unified inference framework and deployment tools, calling Edge0-145B the world’s first open-source on-device AI model with 145 billion parameters. The company says its laptop comparison reports more than 80 tokens per second at a peak memory of roughly 28GB to 29GB, enabling local use on a 48GB laptop. Only about 10 billion of the 145 billion parameters work on each inference step, as groups of 64 experts share two large matrices. Edge0 says the model scored 86.52 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 in its internal evaluations, ahead of several named models, and averages 72.8 across six benchmarks. Its demos include building a 3D Manhattan scene in Blender within an hour, entirely locally. Weights are on Hugging Face, and the Edge0 App’s core capabilities work offline without an account.

title: Nex-AGI releases open weights for Nex-N2.6, a 321-billion-parameter computer-use agent
summary: Nex-AGI has opened model weights for Nex-N2.6, a multimodal agent intended to work through computer interfaces, coding sessions and longer tool-based workflows, Open Model Weights reported Thursday, November 12, 2026. The public Hugging Face repository holds FP8-quantized weights for a roughly 321-billion-parameter model derived from GLM-5.3-Flash and is marked Apache-2.0. The release focuses on agent reliability: choosing only tools that are actually available, avoiding repeated thinking loops and continuing after environmental feedback. Nex-AGI reports an OSWorld score of 83.0, versus 82.2 for Nex-N2.5-Pro and 78.0 for the GLM-5.3-Flash baseline, and 84.1 on Terminal-Bench 2.1; in its internal replay tests, reasoning repetition fell from 16.0% to 1.6%. Open Model Weights notes these are issuer-reported results, and that a checkpoint this size is an infrastructure decision rather than an on-device model.

title: Meta’s Muse AI can now make phone calls to US businesses for paying subscribers
summary: Meta’s Muse can now place calls to U.S. businesses for anyone who pays for the AI, TechCrunch reported Thursday, November 12, 2026. Previously only a select number of early adopters could try the feature after asking the AI for access. Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, said it could handle calls people don’t want to make, like those to a cable company, the DMV or a restaurant that doesn’t take online reservations. Muse plans start at $20 per month for 500 million Muse tokens per week, with a $100 plan for 3 billion tokens. Meta said last month that Muse has more than 10 million users. Muse isn’t the only agent that can call businesses: the startup Instinct and Google’s Gemini offer similar options, though many businesses hang up once they realize a caller isn’t human. Wang said Muse email addresses will soon roll out to free users.

title: Phota Labs launches a free app that reshoots your everyday photos with AI
summary: Phota Labs, an a16z-backed startup founded by former Adobe computational photography developers Cecilia Zhang and Zach Xia, is launching a free app that uses AI to fix the shot itself rather than just edit it, TechCrunch reported Thursday, November 12, 2026. The app can turn a wide-angle group photo into a tighter portrait or a selfie into a regular shot, with styles ranging from subtle edits that keep the original lens to dramatic changes like fish-eye lenses and new angles. Zhang said the company built personalization technology that learns people’s identity so it can preserve them in any transformation. Edited images carry invisible watermarks identifying them as altered by AI when shared on social platforms. Phota raised a $5.6 million seed round led by a16z last year, plans to explore a freemium model and intends to launch an Android app later.

title: Nectar launches a Creator Agent that finds influencers and handles brand outreach
summary: Nectar, founded by sisters and former Meta employees Misbah and Farah Uraizee, on Thursday, November 12, 2026, announced a Creator Agent that can search for creators, check their content and brand partnerships, send personalized messages, coordinate collaborations and monitor campaign results, TechCrunch reported. Nectar says the agent searches more than 300 million creator profiles, including smaller creators gaining traction, and analyzes videos in context to check brand safety. It can draft messages in a brand’s voice, build landing pages and help manage contracts, gifting and shipping, and it flags personal milestones like a new baby or a finished marathon to suggest a gift. The agent is available globally for Instagram and TikTok creators and will come to AI assistants like Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot through MCP. U.S. creator ad spending is expected to reach $44 billion in 2026, per the Interactive Advertising Bureau.

title: An AI agent swarm’s ‘unmapped’ Maya site turned out to be already published
summary: Google researcher Pietro Miotti said this week that a team of 48 AI agents combing NASA lidar data in a personal side project had flagged a potentially unmapped Maya site in Mexico, but the site had already been documented in an academic journal last year, The Verge reported Thursday, November 12, 2026. Miotti, who checked with Mexico’s National Institute of Anthropology and History, later said that as a non-archaeologist he hadn’t realized an unregistered site wasn’t the same as an unmapped one and that expert knowledge “is needed to verify what the agents find.” Archaeologists pushed back: University of Alabama at Birmingham professor Sarah Parcak wrote, “This is why we have peer review,” and University College London’s Elizabeth Graham said the bigger obstacle is funding to excavate. Still, Miotti said archaeologists and PhD students have asked whether his workflow could help with their own survey data.

title: A South African teen used machine learning to test whether an invasive weed can help crops grow
summary: Grade 11 student Rudra Patel of the University of Johannesburg Academy Maths, Science and ICT School of Specialisation won a Gold Medal, the Top Senior Scientist Award and the CambriLearn Built For How You Think Award at the 46th Eskom Expo for Young Scientists International Science Fair 2026, India Today reported Thursday, November 12, 2026. The Top Senior Scientist Award carried a prize of R75,000 (about Rs 4.1 lakh). His project built machine-learning models to predict how extracts of Lantana camara, an invasive alien plant, might affect wheat seedlings, then tested them in the lab; the models were less reliable under independent conditions, showing machine learning can’t yet replace lab testing. Patel admitted considering giving up several times while juggling exams and a trip to the Regeneron ISEF in May, but support from his mentor, friends and family helped him persevere. He plans to save the prize for university.

title: A Surat schoolboy’s AI groundwater forecaster wins India’s vivo Ignite 2026
summary: Surat school student Dheyay Shah won the top award in the fourth edition of vivo Ignite 2026, a nationwide innovation challenge for school students, for JALAAKAR – The Shape of Water: Predict, Alert, and Act, Education Times reported Tuesday, November 10, 2026. JALAAKAR is a machine-learning project that analyzes historical borewell, rainfall and soil data to estimate groundwater availability at the taluka level, which could help communities and farming regions make informed decisions about water use. The organizers have not shared details on the model’s accuracy or independent testing. The national final recognized 13 young innovators for 10 ideas on water conservation, pollution control, women’s safety, road safety and assistive technology, including a LiDAR-enabled safety collar for visually impaired people. This edition drew more than 38,000 registrations and over 6,100 ideas from more than 12,000 schools across 705 districts.

title: Roger Guenveur Smith brings his Frederick Douglass monologue to the Theater at Baranco tonight
summary: Performing Arts Serving Acadiana presents Frederick Douglass on Friday, November 13, 2026, from 7:30 to 9:30 p.m. at the Theater at Baranco, 801 Mudd Avenue in Lafayette. Roger Guenveur Smith returns to perform the theatrical monologue inspired by the life and work of Frederick Douglass, the self-liberated abolitionist and pioneering feminist, editing Douglass’s 19th-century texts into a jazz-infused narrative bookended by his own writing. The play runs approximately 60 minutes with no intermission. Tickets are listed at $16.88 to $32 through PASA’s ticketing page.

title: Shakespeare’s Othello opens tonight at Cité des Arts with a gala, with shows through Sunday
summary: Cité des Arts opens its production of Othello by William Shakespeare, the fourth play in its 2026 theater season, on Friday, November 13, 2026, with an opening night gala at 6:30 p.m. featuring noshes and signature cocktails, followed by the show at 7:30 p.m. Opening night general admission is $35. Performances continue Saturday, November 14, at 7:30 p.m. and Sunday, November 15, at 2:00 p.m., with general admission at $25, and return Friday, November 20, and Saturday, November 21, at 7:30 p.m. Cité des Arts calls Othello one of Shakespeare’s greatest tragedies, the story of a noble Moorish general whose life and marriage are destroyed by manipulation, envy and treachery. Cité des Arts is at 109 Vine St. in Lafayette.

title: Cajun Cup 10K and Farrel’s Mile hit Parc Sans Souci Saturday morning
summary: The Cajun Road Runners Club’s Cajun Cup 10K and Farrel’s Mile take place Saturday, November 14, 2026, at Parc Sans Souci in Lafayette, with the 1-mile at 7:30 a.m. and the 10K at 8:05 a.m. The race is a fundraiser supporting the Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns cross country and track teams. Online registration closes Saturday at 7:00 a.m., and in-person registration is available at packet pickup and on race morning until 7:00 a.m. Age groups run in five-year increments starting with 9 and under, and the course closes at about two hours. A shoe drive for Lafayette Catholic Services will have collection boxes at Geaux Run on Friday and at the race Saturday morning. Swag is pickup only.

title: Downtown Lafayette’s November ArtWalk lights up galleries and studios Saturday night
summary: Downtown Lafayette’s November ArtWalk takes place Saturday, November 14, 2026, from 5:00 to 9:00 p.m. ArtWalk happens every second Saturday of the month, rain or shine. Downtown Lafayette says no single organization plans the activities; instead, each museum, gallery and studio hosts its own event featuring local artists and performers, and visitors can follow the official ArtWalk Lafayette Facebook page for the month’s lineup. Downtown Lafayette partners with Lafayette Arts & Fleas to highlight local talent, and artisans interested in vending at future ArtWalks can email lafartsfleas@gmail.com.

title: The Lafayette Farmers & Artisans Market fills Moncus Park Saturday morning
summary: The Lafayette Farmers & Artisans Market runs every Saturday from 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. at Moncus Park, rain or shine, including Saturday, November 14, 2026. Moncus Park says the market transforms the heart of the park into a gathering place where local farmers, artisans and craftspeople share the best of the region, and it currently hosts more than 150 vendors. The vendor list is posted on the market’s Facebook page the Friday before market day. Parking at Moncus Park is $2 per hour, or free for members, with proceeds supporting the nonprofit park conservancy; the park warns that towing is strictly enforced in neighboring lots. Moncus Park is at 2913 Johnston Street.
